refnamediv.refpurpose: APIs for encrypting and decrypting service credentials.

refsect1.title: Description
refsect1.para: io.systemd.Credentials is a Varlink interface implemented by systemd1-related components. It can be introspected and called with varlinkctl1.
APIs for encrypting and decrypting service credentials.

refsect1.title: Interface Definition
refsect1.para: The following interface definition is exposed:
refsect1.programlisting:
# APIs for encrypting and decrypting service credentials. interface io.systemd.Credentials
# The intended scope for the credential. type Scope( # Generate a system-bound credential system, # Generate a system and user bound credential user )
# Selects the key(s) to encrypt the credentials with. type WithKey( # Automatically pick the key to bind the credential to auto, # Automatically pick the key to bind the credential to, but ensure it is accessible in the initrd, thus potentially leaving it unencrypted. auto_initrd, # Bind to the host key only, i.e. not the TPM host, # Bind to the TPM only, not the host key tpm2, # Bind to the TPM only (using a public key identifying the UKI), not the host key tpm2_with_public_key, # Bind to both the TPM and the host key host_tpm2, # Bind to both the TPM (using a public key identifying the UKI) and the host key host_tpm2_with_public_key, # Do not bind to either host key nor the TPM, thus using null encryption (this provides no authenticity nor confidentiality guarantees) null )
# Encrypts some plaintext data, returns an encrypted credential. method Encrypt( # The name for the encrypted credential, a string suitable for inclusion in a file name. If not specified no name is encoded in the credential. Typically, if this credential is stored on disk, this is how the file should be called, and permits authentication of the filename. name: ?string, # Plaintext to encrypt. Suitable only for textual data. Either this field or 'data' (below) must be provided. text: ?string, # Plaintext to encrypt, encoded in Base64. Suitable for binary data. Either this field or 'text' (above) must be provided. data: ?string, # Timestamp to store in the credential. In µs since the UNIX epoch, i.e. Jan 1st 1970. If not specified the current time is used. timestamp: ?int, # Timestamp when to the credential should be considered invalid. In µs since the UNIX epoch. If not specified, the credential remains valid forever. notAfter: ?int, # The intended scope for the credential. One of 'system' or 'user'. If not specified defaults to 'system', unless an uid is specified (see below), in which case it default to 'user'. scope: ?Scope, # Selects the type of key to encrypt this with withKey: ?WithKey, # The numeric UNIX UID of the user the credential shall be scoped to. Only relevant if 'user' scope is selected (see above). If not specified and 'user' scope is selected defaults to the UID of the calling user, if that can be determined. uid: ?int, # Controls whether interactive authentication (via polkit) shall be allowed. If unspecified defaults to false. allowInteractiveAuthentication: ?bool ) -> ( # Encrypted credential in Base64 encoding. This can be stored in a credential file, for consumption in LoadEncryptedCredential= and similar calls. Note that the Base64 encoding should be retained when copied into a file. blob: string )
# Decrypts an encrypted credential, returns plaintext data. method Decrypt( # The name of the encrypted credential. Must the same string specified when the credential was encrypted, in order to authenticate this. If not specified authentication of the credential name is not done. name: ?string, # The encrypted credential in Base64 encoding. This corresponds of the 'blob' field returned by the 'Encrypt' method. blob: string, # The timestamp to use when validating the credential's time validity range. If not specified the current time is used. timestamp: ?int, # The scope for this credential. If not specified no restrictions on the credential scope are made. scope: ?Scope, # If the 'user' scope is selected, specifies the numeric UNIX UID of the user the credential is associated with. If not specified this is automatically derived from the UID of the calling user, if that can be determined. uid: ?int, # If true allows decryption of credentials encrypted with the null key, if false does not allow it, if unset/null the default depends on whether a TPM device exists and SecureBoot is enabled. allowNull: ?bool, # Controls whether interactive authentication (via polkit) shall be allowed. If unspecified defaults to false. allowInteractiveAuthentication: ?bool ) -> ( # The decrypted plaintext data in Base64 encoding. data: string )
# Indicates that a corrupt and unsupported encrypted credential was provided. error BadFormat()
# The specified name does not match the name stored in the credential. error NameMismatch()
# The credential's is no longer or not yet valid. error TimeMismatch()
# The specified user does not exist. error NoSuchUser()
# The credential does not match the selected scope. error BadScope()
# PCR signature required for decryption, but not found. error CantFindPCRSignature()
# The key was encrypted with a null key, but that's not allowed during decryption. error NullKeyNotAllowed()
# The TPM integrity check for this key failed, key probably belongs to another TPM, or was corrupted. error KeyBelongsToOtherTPM()
# The TPM is in dictionary lockout mode, cannot operate. error TPMInDictionaryLockout()
# Unexpected TPM PCR state of the system. error UnexpectedPCRState()
# The NV index referenced by the key is missing, unwritten, or unusable, it could be for another system. error NVIndexUnusable()

refsect1.title: Examples
refsect1.para: varlinkctl introspect SERVICE io.systemd.Credentials shows the interface definition as served by SERVICE, and varlinkctl call SERVICE io.systemd.Credentials.Encrypt '{}' invokes its Encrypt method.
